title: wildcat infrastructure offers buy austals us operations up 135 billion 2026 09 09
text:
Sept 9 (Reuters) - Australian shipbuilder Austal (ASB.AX)
, opens new tab
 said on Wednesday U.S.-based Wildcat Infrastructure had offered up to $1.35 billion for its U.S. business, topping a bid from South Korea's Hanwha Group ​and sending its shares sharply higher.
The competing proposals come as Washington tries ​to rebuild naval capacity and lift submarine production, increasing the value ⁠of assets such as Austal USA.
With existing shipyards, a skilled workforce and ​defence relationships, Austal USA is among a small group of operators capable of ​supporting Washington's efforts.
"I think what buyers see in Austal USA is its scarcity value, particularly against the backdrop of ongoing geopolitical tensions and the conflict with Iran," said Cliff Man, ​CEO at ETF shares.
Austal shares closed 7.1% higher after rising as much as ​9% to A$4.74, their highest in nearly a month.
Wildcat offered $1.25 billion to $1.35 ‌billion ⁠for Austal USA on a cash-free, debt-free basis, subject to four weeks of due diligence, topping Hanwha's bid of up to $1.20 billion made a month ago.
Hanwha Group declined to comment when contacted by Reuters.
In December, the Australian government approved Hanwha's proposal ​to raise its stake ​in Austal to ⁠19.9% from 9.9%, subject to conditions on data access and security.
Austal's shipbuilding footprint spans four countries, with five shipyards ​in Australia, the U.S., the Philippines and Vietnam.
Florida-based private investment ​firm Wildcat ⁠Infrastructure said it intends to operate the business as a standalone platform while retaining the Austal brand and its U.S. operations.
Austal's U.S. business segment reported an earnings ⁠before ​interest and taxes loss of A$202.8 million ($146.50 million) ​for the 2026 financial year.
($1 = 1.3843 Australian dollars)
